主要内容: The global oil and gas midstream market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 1.9% from 2020 to 2026, with the global operating oil and gas pipeline length expected to increase from 2,079.72 thousand km in 2020 to 2,353.86 thousand km by 2026. The midstream sector was relatively unaffected by the COVID-19 pandemic due to the continued use of storage facilities, pipelines for fuel transportation, and resilient demand for LNG. Factors such as increasing production and consumption of natural gas and refined petroleum products are expected to drive demand for pipeline services. However, environmental concerns regarding new pipeline and transportation infrastructure may restrain market growth. The transportation segment is expected to dominate the market due to rising demand for refined products. South America is anticipated to be the fastest-growing market, driven by growing LNG demand in countries like Chile, Brazil, and Argentina. Major pipeline projects in Brazil, such as the Bolivia-Brazil pipeline (GASBOL), are expected to increase pipeline capacity to 3.6 million cubic meters by 2022. South and Central America imported 13.9 billion cubic meters of LNG in 2020, a 5.4% increase from 2019. The oil and gas midstream market is expected to grow during the forecast period (2021-2026) due to the development of new projects. In the country, there are 10 projects in the licensing phase, 11 in the initial study phase, and two under construction. These developments are anticipated to boost the midstream market in the region. The market is moderately fragmented, with key players such as APA Group, Chevron Corporation, BP PLC, Enbridge Pipelines Inc., and Royal Dutch Shell PLC.
